catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 binds robot.arm or motion.axis and takes joint positions in radians; the Franka Hand MoveAction takes a parallel-finger opening in metres and a speed and binds robot.gripper. No catalogue class expresses moving a robot.gripper to a width.

No catalogue class homes or calibrates a robot.gripper. cap.device.configure.v1 is a resource-state write, while the upstream HomingAction performs a physical reference motion with its own action result.
cap.motion.stop.v1 binds robot.arm, robot.mobile_base or motion.axis, not robot.gripper. This extension binds the gripper's fixed actionlib StopAction as its independently confirmed safety route.

WHY HELPER_MISSING (stop path). The only upstream gripper stop is the actionlib StopAction server on the relative name "stop" (franka_gripper/src/franka_gripper_node.cpp:101-105), whose handler calls gripper.stop() (franka_gripper/src/franka_gripper.cpp:90-92). RosDriver safety bindings accept only acknowledged ROS service calls: mhs/bridge/ros.py rejects an action there, and an Action(safe_state=True) is still rejected when its command binding is an action. Minimal repro: RosBridge({"safety_bindings": {"estop": {"action": "/franka_gripper/stop", "type": "franka_gripper/StopAction", "profile": "ros1-actionlib", "success": {"path": "success", "equals": true}}}}) raises MHSError "safety_bindings.estop: actions are command bindings, never reads, writes or safety bindings". The clone's only service-shaped stop is the franka_gazebo set_user_stop std_srvs/SetBool service (franka_gazebo/src/franka_hw_sim.cpp:405-411), and the vendor text calls it a special service only available in franka_gazebo to simulate the user stop (franka_gazebo/doc/index.rst:230-234); it is not installed by the hardware node. The clone exposes no independent hardware e-stop line for the gripper. A direct Driver over the C++ ROS node would need a fabricated Python native, which the rules exclude. The seven-axis arm's primary motion is streamed through external ros_control controller interfaces and has no acknowledged in-clone motion service; I did not replace that control with an observation-only arm driver. No honest @estop, safety_bindings.estop or safe_state.achieved_by exists for this hardware device, so the package is not a completed integration.

WHAT IS COVERED. The partial declaration is for the Franka Hand gripper, not the arm: the grasp, move, homing and stop actionlib servers and the /franka_gripper/joint_states sensor_msgs/JointState observation. Units are converted in the production binding: class width mm -> Grasp/MoveAction width m, force N unchanged, and the two finger positions are the values from the node. Four bounds are Limit.operator_required because no clone line states a maximum opening, grasp force or speed: the node reports max_width at run time and default_speed/default_grasp_epsilon are configurable ROS parameters (franka_gripper/config/franka_gripper_node.yaml:1-5), not device limits. site-limits.example.json is an example overlay only, not a fact, and every call carrying those fields is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until an operator supplies site-limits.json. The cap.manipulation.grasp.v1 class's optional approach field is inherited in the generated schema but not mapped, because GraspAction has no approach goal field; a caller that sends it is ignored. The reference was regenerated after the last driver change.

FAKE. fake.py is a ROS-free analytic stand-in, not a recording and not the Gazebo plugin. It models the actionlib goal/status/result wire and the JointState subscription with placeholder values, each marked # placeholder; the node's 30 Hz publication rate and the result shapes follow the cited source, but no contact physics, Gazebo world, ROS graph or hardware behavior is modeled. It is F0 contract evidence only, never an MHS-Device level, and fake evidence does not establish a real ROS or hardware run.

SAFETY AND PROVENANCE. Risk is R2 for the pinch/force hazard, above the card floor R0 and the cap.manipulation.grasp.v1 class floor R1. No physical e-stop is claimed or cited. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is {"kind": "model", "model_id": "deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017", "run_id": "mhs-ros-continuation-20261102-a-001"} and reviewed_by stays null. A model-authored R2 package never runs its hardware backend until a human signs reviewed_by; RosDriver additionally refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review, and no hardware was attached. No human reviewed or tested anything and no hardware run is claimed. Every Fact cites the pinned clone; G4 passed with no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warning. The clone was left unmodified (git status clean), the SDK was not edited, no network or pip install was used, and no upstream code was imported, installed or run. The G7.ROS_NO_MESSAGES warning is expected: the fake transport records no outbound message because G6 did not run after the G3 stop failure.
